% Regression: t2_olvert — renders (O_L(M))_{(l_1..l_L),(r_1..r_L)}.
% t2_olvert — RMP arXiv:2011.12127, Eq. (Fig:MPDO-O_L), file
% fig2_fig2-pepe_MPDO-O_L.pdf: the MPO O_L generated by the MPDO tensor
% M by contracting the same tensors VERTICALLY on a ring of length L.
% Revisits hard05, whose v2 could only draw the ring rotated 90 degrees
% and anticipated a `chain axis` spelling; both keys now exist.
%
% Formula:  (O_L(M))_{(l_1..l_L),(r_1..r_L)}
%             = Tr[ M(l_1,r_1) M(l_2,r_2) ... M(l_L,r_L) ],
% where M(l,r) is the MPDO tensor M read as a matrix on its physical
% index pair, the trace runs over the vertical chain of physical
% indices (the ring closure), and each site's virtual indices l_j, r_j
% stay open — they are the physical legs of the MPO O_L.
%
% Declarative reading:
%   chain axis=south       — the word descends: the RMP's vertical ring,
%                            \tndots renders \vdots;
%   physical=updown        — each M keeps its own transverse leg pair
%                            (M's virtual indices), pointing west/east
%                            after the frame map;
%   periodic, trace style=hooks   — the ring seen edge-on: at each end of the
%                            traced word the wire turns a near-semicircle
%                            toward the return side, return wire implied
%                            (the key's own reference is this figure).
% Boundary signature: the chain wire is CLOSED (periodic), one
% transverse pair per drawn site stays open — O_L is an operator.
\documentclass[varwidth=19cm, border=6pt]{standalone}
\usepackage{amsmath, amssymb}
\usepackage{tenkz}
\begin{document}
\[
  O_L(M) \;=\;
  \begin{tenkz}[chain axis=south, physical=updown, periodic, trace style=hooks,
                tensor style=box]
    \tn{M} & \tndots & \tn{M}
  \end{tenkz}
\]
\end{document}
